Each request is one small log line (about 1 KB), so 34 GB means tens of millions of requests or log lines on Nov 16. Something was sending traffic in a loop or at very high volume.\n\n**New lead: the `landing` site (Next.js on Vercel, folder `PoolPal/landing`).**\n- It uses the same Supabase project as the app (`tmfydyxmqgfxahodvvjh`).\n- It was created on Nov 16 (git history: \"Initial commit from Create Next App\" at 20:48 +0500, landing page at 21:05). If the project\u0027s JWT signing key is the legacy HS256 secret, `getClaims()` calls `/auth/v1/user` on the Auth server every time. If the token is expired, it refreshes via `/auth/v1/token`. Crawlers, bots or `\u003cLink\u003e` prefetches with a session cookie would each produce Auth log lines. Running `next dev` locally multiplies requests too.\n2. **Browser and middleware both refreshing the same refresh token.** `landing/providers/auth-provider.tsx` plus `proxy.ts` can race on token rotation and produce repeated `refresh_token_already_used` errors and retries. This is speculative.\n3. **`landing/providers/auth-provider.tsx:17-32`.** `onAuthStateChange` sets a new `user` object on every event, and the effect re-runs `fetchProfile` (`profiles` select) each time. This is bounded, not an infinite loop, but it multiplies REST calls per auth event.\n4. **`startCheckout` calling `create-checkout-session` (`landing/lib/supabase.ts:34-46`).** It is clicked by a user, and the button is disabled while pending. It cannot loop by itself. The function writes 5 to 8 log lines per call, so 34 GB would need tens of millions of calls. That would require a bot, a script, or someone hitting the public function URL directly. It also makes Stripe calls per invocation. I rate this unlikely on its own.\n5. **External abuse.** The landing `signUp`, sign-in and checkout endpoints are public. A bot hitting `/auth/v1/signup` or `/functions/v1/create-checkout-session` would produce this kind of volume.\n\nI cannot confirm which one from code alone.
